narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high temperature of 29°C (84°F) is expected today before dropping to a low of 19°C (66°F) tonight. Skies remain partly cloudy early and through midday, turning mostly cloudy by evening. Wind blows from the SW at midday with peak gusts reaching 41 km/h (22 kt) ashore. Evening Showers & Thunderstorms are expected with onset from 19:00, bringing 12.7 mm (0.50 in) of rain with 100% chance, and thunder possible, peaking this evening. The peak UV index reaches 9.2 today. Air quality is an AQI 80 model estimate.

## Extended Outlook

Cooling through Friday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Wednesday, and rain and thunderstorms possible from Thursday. Skies overcast throughout. Friday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 22 to 24°C (71 to 76°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 87% of the time over 87 checks.

Further out, warming through Tuesday, with showers and thunderstorms possible Saturday, rain and thunderstorms likely Sunday and Monday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Tuesday. Saturday: all four models wet, highs 24 to 27°C (74 to 80°F). Sunday: all four models wet, highs around 26°C (79°F), thunder likely rather than possible. Monday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 28°C (82°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Sunday. GFS is the wetter solution from Saturday to Sunday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Tuesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 27°C (81°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 83 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunderstorms are possible ahead as CAPE values peak at 18:00, reaching 1010 J/kg in GFS, 2220 J/kg in ECMWF, 1520 J/kg in ICON, 5740 J/kg in UKMO, and 1800 J/kg in Best Match. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No met service warning is currently active.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

On Winam Gulf, wind moves overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 20 km/h (11 kt), then into the evening at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 14 km/h (8 kt); peak gust 32 km/h (17 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, they bring the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1013 hPa) and highest toward the southwest (1016 hPa) — a 3 hPa spread, a weak large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the northwest, south — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1015.4 and 1017.5 hPa; near-steady over three days (-0.2 hPa). Pressure shows a trend of +0.5 hPa, with a weak large-scale gradient and lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet across 67 checks, though GFS holds the best rain record, right 90% of the last 30 checks. Model biases show GFS slightly over-forecasts daytime highs and cloud cover, under-forecasts peak wind, and historically does not see thunderstorms coming. ECMWF and Best Match slightly under-forecast daytime highs and peak wind. ICON slightly under-forecasts highs and over-forecasts cloud cover. Today's call sets a high of 29°C (84°F) and low of 19°C (66°F), sitting within model spreads (highs 28.8–30.3°C [83.8–86.5°F], lows 17.5–21.6°C [63.5–70.9°F]). The call's 12.7 mm (0.50 in) rain call sits near ECMWF (11.3 mm [0.44 in]) and UKMO (12.5 mm [0.49 in]), while ICON calls 24.8 mm (0.98 in) and Best Match calls 3.6 mm (0.14 in). Peak gust call of 41 km/h (22 kt) aligns near ECMWF (40 km/h [22 kt]) and Best Match (46.8 km/h [25 kt]), while GFS sits on the wrong side of its wind bias calling only 13.3 km/h (7 kt). No bulletin came from the Kenya Meteorological Department. Data sufficiency is settled with 90 days of stored forecasts reviewed and 67 checks for the least-covered model.
